cards.heading: decentralized finance
cards.body: DeFi replaces banks with code. Smart contracts on blockchains like Ethereum handle lending, trading, and earning — no middleman, no office hours, no permission needed.

cards.text: DeFi doesn't mean 'no rules' — it means the rules are written in code that anyone can read and verify.

cards.heading: your keys, your coins
cards.body: A crypto wallet stores your private keys — the passwords that prove you own your assets. Unlike a bank account, nobody can freeze or seize your wallet.

cards.text: Never share your seed phrase. Not with 'support', not on a website, not in a DM. Ever.

cards.heading: the cost of computation
cards.body: Every transaction on a blockchain costs gas — a small fee paid to validators who process your request. More complex actions (like swaps) cost more gas than simple transfers.

cards.heading: why gas prices change
cards.body: Gas is priced by demand. When many people transact at once, gas spikes. L2 chains like Base batch transactions to Ethereum, making gas 50-100x cheaper.

cards.text: On Base, a typical swap costs less than $0.01. The same swap on Ethereum L1 can cost $5-50+.

cards.heading: ethereum, but faster and cheaper
cards.body: Base is a Layer 2 (L2) chain built by Coinbase. It inherits Ethereum's security while processing transactions faster and cheaper. Your assets on Base are secured by Ethereum.

cards.heading: why builders choose Base
cards.body: Low fees, fast confirmations, Coinbase ecosystem distribution, and a growing community of apps and users. Over 100M transactions processed.

cards.text: Base is open-source, permissionless, and decentralized. Anyone can build on it.

cards.heading: what happens when you tap 'send'
cards.body:
1. You sign the transaction with your private key.
2. It enters the mempool (waiting room).
3. A validator picks it up and includes it in a block.
4. The block is confirmed — your transaction is final.

cards.heading: reading a transaction
cards.body: Every tx has: sender (from), receiver (to), value, gas used, gas price, status (success/fail), and a unique hash. You can view any tx on BaseScan.

cards.text: Try it: open basescan.org, paste any address, and explore the transaction history. Everything is public.
